programmes.name_local: Basic Education Employment Initiative (BEEI) / Presidential Youth Employment
programmes.funder: Department of Basic Education (funded by National Treasury and UIF)
programmes.amount_note: Short-term contracts as education assistants, general school assistants and eCadres in public schools, paid a monthly stipend (about R4,000/month in recent phases, less for part-time). Phase 5 (2025) created 204,676 opportunities for youth 18-34.
programmes.deadline_note: Phases are announced; applications via SAYouth.mobi (zero-rated)

procedure_steps.detail: Register on SAYouth.mobi and apply when a BEEI phase opens
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed at schools and sign fixed-term contracts

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Matric certificate (for education assistants)

eligibility.income_note: Unemployed youth 18-34; must live near the school

programmes.source_snippet: Phase 5 of the Basic Education Employment Initiative (BEEI) was launched in June 2025, creating 204 676 job opportunities for youth aged 18-34

programmes.funder: YES (private sector initiative, B-BBEE incentive for companies)
programmes.amount_note: 12-month paid quality work experience for unemployed youth 18-35 at host companies, paid at least the national minimum wage; participating companies gain B-BBEE level recognition.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the YES4Youth platform and apply to host-company placements

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Matric or higher (varies by placement)

eligibility.income_note: Unemployed black youth 18-34 prioritised

programmes.source_snippet: YES gives youth a 12-month quality work experience and gives businesses B-BBEE level ups for creating youth jobs

programmes.funder: Unemployment Insurance Fund (Department of Employment and Labour)
programmes.amount_note: 38%-58% of your previous salary (lower earners get a higher percentage), capped at a remuneration ceiling of R17,712/month; payable for up to 365 days depending on credits (1 day per 4 days worked).
programmes.deadline_note: Claim within 12 months of becoming unemployed (best practice: as soon as possible)

procedure_steps.detail: Register and claim on the uFiling portal (ufiling.labour.gov.za) or visit a Labour Centre
Submit the relevant UI form and supporting documents
UIF pays benefits into your bank account once approved

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
UI application form (e.g. UI-2.8 for banking details)
Proof of unemployment / employer confirmation (UI-19)

eligibility.income_note: Must have contributed to UIF while employed; must be available for work; not for resignation or misconduct dismissal in some cases

programmes.source_snippet: UIF benefit payments capped at R17,712/month. Benefits: 38%-58% of salary. Max claim period: up to 365 days

programmes.funder: Unemployment Insurance Fund (Department of Employment and Labour)
programmes.amount_note: 38%-58% of salary (capped at the R17,712/month ceiling) for up to 121 days (4 months) of maternity leave for contributors; also for miscarriage/stillbirth and commissioning parents.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before or within 12 months after the birth

procedure_steps.detail: Register and claim on the uFiling portal (ufiling.labour.gov.za) or visit a Labour Centre
Submit the relevant UI form and supporting documents
UIF pays benefits into your bank account once approved

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Maternity leave confirmation from employer
Medical certificate / birth certificate

eligibility.income_note: UIF contributors; can be claimed even if employer pays partial salary (top-up to ceiling)

programmes.source_snippet: Contributors on maternity leave can claim up to 121 days of UIF maternity benefits

programmes.funder: Unemployment Insurance Fund (Department of Employment and Labour)
programmes.amount_note: 38%-58% of salary (capped at the R17,712/month ceiling) when a contributor cannot work due to illness for more than 14 days and receives reduced or no pay.
programmes.deadline_note: Claim within 12 months of the illness period

procedure_steps.detail: Register and claim on the uFiling portal (ufiling.labour.gov.za) or visit a Labour Centre
Submit the relevant UI form and supporting documents
UIF pays benefits into your bank account once approved

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Medical certificate
Employer confirmation of reduced pay (UI-19)

eligibility.income_note: UIF contributors unable to work due to illness

programmes.source_snippet: Illness benefits are paid to contributors who cannot work because of illness for more than two weeks

programmes.funder: Unemployment Insurance Fund (Department of Employment and Labour)
programmes.amount_note: 38%-58% of the deceased contributor's salary (capped at the R17,712/month ceiling) paid to the surviving spouse/life partner, then dependent children, of a deceased UIF contributor.
programmes.deadline_note: Spouse must apply within 18 months of the contributor's death

procedure_steps.detail: Register and claim on the uFiling portal (ufiling.labour.gov.za) or visit a Labour Centre
Submit the relevant UI form and supporting documents
UIF pays benefits into your bank account once approved

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Death certificate of the contributor
Marriage certificate / proof of dependency

eligibility.income_note: Dependants of a deceased UIF contributor

programmes.source_snippet: The dependants of a deceased contributor can claim UIF benefits from the Fund

programmes.funder: Unemployment Insurance Fund (Department of Employment and Labour)
programmes.amount_note: 38%-58% of salary (capped at the R17,712/month ceiling) for contributors who legally adopt a child under two years old and take adoption leave; only one adopting parent may claim.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply within 12 months of the adoption order

procedure_steps.detail: Register and claim on the uFiling portal (ufiling.labour.gov.za) or visit a Labour Centre
Submit the relevant UI form and supporting documents
UIF pays benefits into your bank account once approved

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Court adoption order

eligibility.income_note: UIF contributors adopting a child under the age of two

programmes.source_snippet: Contributors who adopt a child under the age of two can claim adoption benefits

programmes.name_local: Compensation Fund (COIDA) - Occupational Injuries and Diseases
programmes.funder: Compensation Fund (Department of Employment and Labour)
programmes.amount_note: No-fault compensation for workplace injuries and occupational diseases: free medical treatment, temporary and permanent disablement pensions (up to 75% of earnings), and dependants' benefits on death. Funded entirely by employer assessments; claiming is free.
programmes.deadline_note: Employer must report within 7 days; claims within 12 months of injury/diagnosis

procedure_steps.detail: Report the injury to your employer immediately; employer files W.CL.2 with the Compensation Fund
Get medical treatment; submit medical reports (W.CL.4, W.CL.5)
The Fund adjudicates and pays medical costs plus disablement/dependants compensation

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Employer's report of accident (W.CL.2)
Medical reports

eligibility.income_note: All employees (employers must be registered with the Fund); no civil claim against employer if covered

programmes.source_snippet: The Compensation Fund is a South African government fund established under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA)

programmes.funder: South African Revenue Service (SARS) / National Treasury
programmes.amount_note: Employers reduce monthly PAYE by the calculated ETI for qualifying young employees (18-29, earning under R7,500/month): up to R1,500/month per employee in the first 12 qualifying months and up to R750/month in the second 12 months. Scheme extended to February 2029.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed monthly on the EMP201; unclaimed amounts can be refunded 6-monthly

procedure_steps.detail: Employer checks employee eligibility (age 18-29, valid ID/asylum permit, wage below R7,500/month)
Calculate the ETI per SARS tables each month
Claim against PAYE on the monthly EMP201 declaration

eligibility.income_note: Employee must earn less than R7,500/month; benefit accrues to the employer

programmes.source_snippet: The Monthly Calculated ETI amount per qualifying employee is within the prescribed legislated threshold (SARS ETI tables)

programmes.funder: National Department of Health / provincial health departments
programmes.amount_note: Free services at public clinics and community health centres for everyone (no user fees at primary level), including people with communicable diseases such as HIV and TB. Hospital care is means-tested under the UPFS.

procedure_steps.detail: Go to your nearest public clinic or community health centre with any ID or passport

eligibility.income_note: Free at primary level for all; hospital-level care is means-tested (UPFS)

programmes.source_snippet: Under the NHA framework, irrespective of nationality and migration status: Everyone is entitled to free primary health services, including people with communicable diseases such as HIV and TB

programmes.name_local: Free Health Care for Pregnant Women and Children Under 6
programmes.name_en: Free Maternal and Under-6 Health Care
programmes.amount_note: All health services free of charge at public facilities (including hospitals) for pregnant and lactating women and for children under six, under section 4(3)(a) of the National Health Act and GN 657 of 1994 (excludes medical aid members).

procedure_steps.detail: Present at any public clinic or hospital; no fees may be charged for qualifying patients

eligibility.income_note: Universal for pregnant/lactating women and children under 6, regardless of nationality or documentation status

programmes.source_snippet: Maternity care is an integral component of primary health care and a free health service for pregnant women (National Department of Health maternity care guidelines)

programmes.name_local: Free HIV Testing and Antiretroviral Treatment (ART)
programmes.amount_note: Free HIV testing, counselling and lifelong antiretroviral therapy (including for TB co-infection and prevention of mother-to-child transmission) at all public health facilities - the world's largest ART programme.

procedure_steps.detail: Test at any public clinic; ART is initiated free of charge, often same-day

programmes.source_snippet: Free services include services for ... infectious diseases such as HIV and TB (national free health services policy)

programmes.amount_note: Free TB screening, diagnosis and full course of treatment (including drug-resistant TB) at public health facilities.

procedure_steps.detail: Present with symptoms or for screening at any public clinic; treatment is free

programmes.source_snippet: Free services include services for ... infectious diseases such as HIV and TB (national free health services policy)

programmes.name_local: Free Childhood Immunisation (Expanded Programme on Immunisation - EPI-SA)
programmes.amount_note: All vaccines on the national EPI schedule (BCG, polio, measles, pentavalent, HPV for schoolgirls, etc.) are free at public clinics; the Road-to-Health booklet tracks the schedule.

procedure_steps.detail: Take the child's Road-to-Health booklet to any public clinic on schedule dates

documents_required.doc: Road-to-Health booklet (issued free at birth)

programmes.source_snippet: Immunisation against vaccine-preventable diseases is provided free of charge at public health facilities under the Expanded Programme on Immunisation

programmes.amount_note: Statutory compensation for people injured (or dependants of those killed) in road accidents caused by another driver's negligence: medical expenses, loss of earnings/support (capped for unidentifiable-driver claims) and general damages for serious injury. Funded by the fuel levy; claiming is free.
programmes.deadline_note: Claims generally within 3 years of the accident (2 years for hit-and-run)

procedure_steps.detail: Obtain the accident report and medical records; complete RAF claim forms (RAF 1, RAF 3/4 as applicable)
Lodge the claim with the RAF (direct or via an attorney)
RAF investigates and settles or the matter proceeds to court

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Police accident report
Medical reports / RAF 4 serious injury report
Proof of earnings (for loss of earnings claims)

eligibility.income_note: Anyone injured by negligent driving on SA roads; minors' claims run against different prescription rules

programmes.source_snippet: RAF claims documentation includes RAF 4 Serious Injury Report, employer's certificate showing remuneration, and itemised tax invoices for past medical expenses

programmes.name_local: Legal Aid South Africa (free legal services)
programmes.amount_note: Free legal representation and advice in criminal and qualifying civil matters for people who cannot afford a lawyer (means test: income roughly below R8,200/month single or per household rule-of-thumb; children always qualify).

procedure_steps.detail: Call the toll-free advice line 0800 110 110 or visit a Legal Aid SA office
Pass the means test and be assigned a legal practitioner

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Proof of income (for means test)

eligibility.income_note: Legal Aid SA's official means test (page live 2026): an employed individual must earn less than R9,400 per month after tax — R112,800/year. For a household sharing costs, the combined limit is R10,200/month. Asset tests also apply. Children in criminal matters qualify regardless of means; thresholds are adjusted annually with CPI.

programmes.source_snippet: Legal Aid SA provides legal aid at state expense to those who cannot afford legal representation, subject to a means test

programmes.name_local: Military Veterans Benefits (Department of Military Veterans)
programmes.amount_note: Registered military veterans (and dependants) can access a package of benefits: housing subsidy, free health care at designated facilities, education support/bursaries, pension (needs-based) and burial support.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the national military veterans database at a DMV office
Apply for specific benefits (housing, health, education, pension) once registered

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Proof of military service

eligibility.income_note: Some benefits (pension) are needs-tested; must be listed on the military veterans database

programmes.source_snippet: The Military Veterans Act provides benefits including housing, health care, education support and a pension for qualifying military veterans

programmes.name_local: Free First ID / Smart ID Card and Free Birth Registration
programmes.name_en: Free First ID and Birth Registration
programmes.amount_note: First issue of an ID/smart ID card (at age 16) is free, as is registration of a birth and the first abridged/unabridged birth certificate; re-issues and late registrations attract fees.
programmes.deadline_note: Births must be registered within 30 days to avoid late-registration processes

procedure_steps.detail: Register the birth at Home Affairs (or at the hospital where available) using form BI-24
Apply for a first smart ID card at a Home Affairs office or bank branch partnership when turning 16

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Birth certificate / proof of birth (for first ID)

programmes.source_snippet: First-time applicants receive their smart ID card free of charge; birth registration within 30 days is free

programmes.funder: Small Enterprise Finance Agency (sefa, under DSBD)
programmes.amount_note: Development loan finance for small and micro enterprises (survivalist, micro, small and medium loans, and property/bridging finance), ranging from tens of thousands up to R15 million, at development rates; not a grant - repayable.

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or at a sefa office with business plan, financials and FICA documents
Credit and due-diligence assessment; loan agreement if approved

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Business plan and financial statements / cash-flow projections
Company registration documents

eligibility.income_note: South African-owned SMMEs, prioritising youth, women and township/rural enterprises

programmes.source_snippet: sefa provides financial products and services to survivalist, micro, small and medium enterprises

programmes.name_local: Small Enterprise Development Agency (SEDA) Business Support
programmes.funder: Small Enterprise Development Agency (SEDA, under DSBD)
programmes.amount_note: Free or subsidised non-financial support for small businesses: business advice, business plans, incubation (SETP/technology incubators), export readiness, quality standards and mentoring.

procedure_steps.detail: Approach a SEDA branch/incubator or use the online enquiry service

documents_required.doc: Business registration documents (for some programmes)

programmes.source_snippet: SEDA provides non-financial business development and support services to small enterprises through its national branch network

programmes.name_local: National Youth Development Agency (NYDA) Grant and Voucher Programme
programmes.amount_note: Grant funding and business development vouchers for youth-owned (18-35) enterprises: grants have historically ranged from R1,000 to R250,000 (typically R5,000-R100,000 for micro-enterprises) plus free mentorship and business skills training.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the NYDA ERP portal and complete the online grant application
Attend assessment/business development support; grant paid in tranches on milestone delivery

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Business registration / business plan

eligibility.income_note: Youth-owned businesses (ownership 26%+ by youth aged 18-35)

programmes.source_snippet: The NYDA Grant Programme provides young entrepreneurs with grant funding and business development support to start and grow businesses

programmes.funder: Department of Small Business Development / sefa / SEDA
programmes.amount_note: Blended grant-and-loan support for township and rural micro and small enterprises (informal traders, general dealers, spazas, clothing, automotive repair, bakeries etc.), combining a grant component with sefa development finance plus capacity support.
programmes.deadline_note: Calls for applications opened periodically via sefa/DSBD

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through sefa when a TREP window opens, with business documents

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Business plan / trading permit or registration

eligibility.income_note: Township and rural enterprises

programmes.source_snippet: TREP supports township and rural enterprises through blended finance (grant plus loan) and business development support

programmes.funder: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
programmes.amount_note: Cost-sharing grant of 30%-50% of qualifying investment (up to R50 million) for majority black-owned manufacturers to expand productive capacity, machinery and working capital.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications per dtic incentive guidelines

procedure_steps.detail: Submit application with business plan, B-BBEE and company documents to the dtic
Appraisal and approval; claims paid against verified expenditure

documents_required.doc: Company registration and B-BBEE certificate
Business plan and financials

eligibility.income_note: Majority black-owned and managed manufacturing enterprises

programmes.source_snippet: The Black Industrialists Scheme offers a cost-sharing grant towards capital investment, feasibility studies and business development services

programmes.funder: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
programmes.amount_note: Partial reimbursement of export marketing costs: participation in international trade exhibitions, missions and primary export market research for emerging exporters (including individuals and SMMEs).
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before the event per EMIA guidelines

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to the dtic before the trade show/mission with company and event documentation
Claim reimbursement with proof of expenditure after the event

documents_required.doc: Company registration and tax clearance
Event invoices and proof of travel

eligibility.income_note: Emerging exporters, SMMEs, HDI-owned entities get preferential rates

programmes.source_snippet: EMIA aims to develop export markets for South African goods and services by partially compensating exporters for qualifying marketing costs

programmes.funder: Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development (DALRRD) / provinces
programmes.amount_note: Conditional grant support to smallholder and subsistence farmers delivered by provinces: production inputs, infrastructure (fencing, irrigation), on/off-farm equipment, training and extension services.
programmes.deadline_note: Provincial calls and business-plan approvals each financial year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at your provincial agriculture office with ID, proof of land access and a farm business plan

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Proof of land access (title, PTO or lease)
Farm business plan

eligibility.income_note: Subsistence, smallholder and previously disadvantaged commercial farmers

programmes.source_snippet: CASP provides post-settlement support to targeted beneficiaries of land reform and other producers who have acquired land through private means

programmes.funder: Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development (DALRRD)
programmes.amount_note: Provincial conditional grant boosting food production: production inputs (seeds, fertiliser, equipment) and support for community food gardens, schools and smallholder producers, implemented by provincial departments of agriculture.
programmes.deadline_note: Provincial allocations each financial year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via your provincial department of agriculture or extension officer

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Proof of land access / garden or farm project details

eligibility.income_note: Vulnerable households, subsistence and smallholder producers

programmes.source_snippet: The Ilima/Letsema programme aims to increase food production through support to subsistence, smallholder and household food producers

programmes.funder: Land and Agricultural Development Bank of South Africa (Land Bank) / DALRRD
programmes.amount_note: Blended grant-plus-loan finance for black commercial farmers (grants of roughly 40-60% of project value combined with Land Bank loans) for land acquisition, production and agri-processing.
programmes.deadline_note: Application windows advertised by Land Bank

procedure_steps.detail: Submit a funding application with farm business plan and land/enterprise documents to Land Bank
Credit assessment and blended structuring with DALRRD grant component

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Farm business plan and financials
Proof of land access / purchase agreement

eligibility.income_note: Black (African) farmers with commercially viable projects

programmes.source_snippet: The Blended Finance Scheme combines a government grant with a Land Bank loan to support black commercial farmers

programmes.name_local: PRASA Metrorail Subsidised Commuter Rail Fares
programmes.funder: Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA) / Department of Transport
programmes.amount_note: Heavily state-subsidised commuter rail fares on Metrorail services (single tickets from a few rand; weekly/monthly tickets at deep discounts versus road transport), with concessionary tickets for pensioners on some routes.

procedure_steps.detail: Buy single, return, weekly or monthly tickets at the station or via the PRASA/Metrorail app

eligibility.income_note: Universal fare subsidy; aimed at low-income commuters

programmes.source_snippet: Metrorail commuter rail fares are subsidised by the state to keep commuter rail affordable for low-income passengers

programmes.name_local: Cape Town Dial-a-Ride (transport for persons with disabilities)
programmes.amount_note: Subsidised kerb-to-kerb shared minibus service for registered users with disabilities who cannot use mainstream public transport; nominal fares per trip.
programmes.deadline_note: Registration required; bookings in advance

procedure_steps.detail: Register with the City as a Dial-a-Ride user (medical proof of disability)
Book trips in advance; pay the subsidised fare per trip

documents_required.doc: South African ID (13-digit bar-coded or smart ID)
Medical certificate / proof of disability

eligibility.income_note: For people with disabilities unable to use conventional public transport

programmes.source_snippet: Dial-a-Ride provides subsidised kerb-to-kerb transport for registered persons with disabilities in Cape Town

programmes.funder: Provincial Departments of Education/Transport (national DBE scholar transport policy)
programmes.amount_note: Free state-provided learner transport for qualifying learners who live far from the nearest appropriate public school (typically more than 5 km from the school), delivered by provincial education departments via contracted operators.
programmes.deadline_note: Apply through the school at the start of the school year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply via the school/principal to the provincial education department's scholar transport unit
Route and eligibility are verified; the learner is assigned to a contracted transport route

documents_required.doc: Proof of residence / distance to school
School enrolment confirmation

eligibility.income_note: Eligibility based mainly on distance to nearest school (generally 5 km+)

programmes.source_snippet: Provincial education departments provide scholar transport to learners who live more than a prescribed distance (usually 5 km) from the nearest suitable school
